title: Move the relation without changing it
before: Write a measurement function, choose display projections and normalize inputs in one opening exercise.
after: Read and predict the existing displacement measurement; use a brief normalization return with its explicit threshold.
reason: The learner already has positions and translation. A lighter return establishes what an arrow measures without delaying the later retained-state hinge.

title: Keep the destination and compare routes
before: Create separate summation and travelled-distance functions and assume supplied receivers consume their outputs.
after: Use the installed result calculation, compare route lengths, and inspect the existing counter with the same carriage and drawings.
reason: The current instrument already makes the distinction tangible. A bounded arithmetic edit avoids adding a second route system before Motion.

title: Keep the component along a direction
before: Teach dot product, projection and remainder while several adjacent operations compete for attention.
after: Make the connected gap/projection pair the core, with recombination as its check and the other operations as short returns.
reason: A single live relation supports reuse and an independent check. The critical questions survive without requiring mastery of every nearby instrument.

title: Read a flight from its beginning
before: Construct a sampled projectile trajectory while introducing acceleration and its quadratic position contribution.
after: Read, evaluate and vary the supplied analytic path, using the existing chamber to check one prediction at a time.
reason: The strong spatial encounter can introduce acceleration without consuming the numerical-state lesson that belongs to Motion next.

title: End the command and keep the motion
before: A finite pulse exercise already separates ending force from stopping motion, but its prediction conditions and handoff into the common state study remain implicit.
after: Make one mass-and-duration prediction before contact, keep drag off for the comparison, and carry the force schedule and observed retained velocity into Fields.
reason: A controlled beginning makes the new idea available for reuse without asking the learner to rebuild the engine’s integrator or turning the friction ramp into another required lesson.

title: Give the same field two meanings
before: Two receiver rules are already explicit, but the authored exercise reads as another isolated pair of markers and lacks a small independent prediction.
after: Name position and velocity as the common study state, predict two uniform-field steps, and keep that update convention for the later spring model.
reason: Assignment versus accumulation becomes something the learner can change and predict, while the runner and display remain supplied and museum state stays honestly separate.

title: Make resistance depend on motion
before: Drag is the principal exercise, but work can become a second required lesson and the mass comparison lacks a concrete predicted quantity.
after: Keep one force function and one initial-acceleration prediction, carry it as damping, and leave walking, mower and ring encounters as optional comparisons.
reason: The state-update strand gains one reusable force term without turning every artifact into another assignment or conflating engine force, annotated work and prescribed motion.

title: Returning does not mean stopping
before: The spring lesson already combines restoration and damping, but the carried update from Fields and the learner’s independent prediction remain implicit.
after: Return explicitly to the same small study convention, own the force sum and ordered update, and predict a release before comparing damping from equal beginnings.
reason: The sequence deepens a usable state model rather than restarting with another animation, while preserving the room’s question of return, rest and motion.

title: Keep an offset, change a rate
before: Build another short row of phased markers, then compare its drift with the conveyor backlog.
after: Use the existing paired-dial source edit to halve drift; predict the gap and explain why equal rates preserve it.
reason: A concrete exercise already exists. It makes the earlier rate and phase skills reusable while leaving rods, conveyor and the artistic reference room to offer different kinds of comparison.

title: Allow the reference to answer
before: Write a two-body interaction and compare a fixed source with mutual response.
after: Focus the work on two receiver contributions, unequal masses and the source's omitted response; keep the solver supplied.
reason: The reusable skill is distributing a shared interaction. Naming the stations' different beginnings prevents a misleading comparison and keeps the task smaller than building an orbital solver.

title: Ask what supports a still body
before: Arrange supplied support pads and use a supplied hull calculation before comparing the walker.
after: Use the existing support controls for one prediction, then compare physical support with the walker's commanded movement.
reason: The hall already offers a precise comparison. It can deepen judgement about bodies and models without turning reflection into another geometry or gait-building task.

title: Ask what an encounter keeps
before: Write a nearest-eligible selector and completed-meal counter alongside the creature encounter.
after: Compare the existing selector, event history and authored stopping rule; test one occlusion prediction without building a controller.
reason: The encounter can develop a careful reading of agency and retained state. An additional implementation obligation would crowd that work and blur its distinction from the separate collision model.

title: Declare what receives the field
before: Compose a cube's field acceleration and compare its receiver with the visitor crossing.
after: Make membership, units and retained velocity explicit, then mark the next hall's deliberate change to descent without velocity.
reason: The closing field should prepare a reusable question about receivers, rather than suggest that Form Finding is another force simulation with the same state.
